reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because a speaker at a OneCoin promotional event predicts that the coin's value will rise, presents account-based opportunities to acquire it at a stated opening price, and encourages network-marketing participation associated with making money. It also claims that account-associated coins are backed by gold and that physical coins could be requested, while those claims are unverified.

opening.argument: The remarks describe a forecast and plans, not a guaranteed return. The speaker says the coin's value will rise if it is pushed, and expresses hope that more exchanges will list it; neither statement establishes that appreciation or additional listings are certain. The talk also acknowledges that mining difficulty changes over time and describes the trading platform and opening price as forthcoming. Read carefully, this is a promotional presentation containing projections and proposed steps, not evidence that a return was promised or realized.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats a prediction, an account-based purchase opportunity, and a hoped-for listing as proof of deceptive solicitation. But those quotes establish what the presenter said, not that appreciation was guaranteed, that the proposed listing occurred, or that any viewer was induced to pay. The presentation also gives technical and operational context, including an auditor's stated independence; the record does not establish that the forecast or proposed arrangements were fulfilled.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the remarks forecasts does not remove their promotional force: the speaker directly says the coin's value will go up when it is pushed, alongside buying opportunities and an opening price. The auditor's claimed independence concerns a blockchain review, not the investment claims or the proposed gold backing, and the supplied material does not independently establish those claims.

opening.argument: This footage is structured as a live presentation explaining how the proposed cryptocurrency system is supposed to work: mining, blockchain consistency, exchange trading, and the relationship between the coin and a gold product. The auditor segment describes specific review objectives, including whether transactions can be traced to the first block. That operational explanation is materially different from showing a viewer how to deposit funds or promising a personal return. The event setting and technical subject matter support reading it as an informational demonstration, even though it includes optimistic promotional claims.

the assessment of the consistency of the blockchain.
All the transactions are valid and could be traced to the very first one

rebuttal.rebuttal: The event's technical explanation is not itself a purchase instruction. The blockchain segment describes audit objectives, while the opening relies on other remarks about a rising value, account buying opportunities, and networking. Those statements still do not establish that anyone was asked to deposit money, that returns were assured, or that a promised outcome occurred. A promotional event can explain a product without proving deception.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical material does not make the video merely a tutorial: the same presentation promotes an exchange, a starting price, rising value, and use of coins on a casino and sports-betting platform. The audit objectives are described by the speaker; they do not establish that the system was independently verified or that the promotional claims were reliable.

opening.argument: The video presents a business and product launch: a proposed exchange listing, a trading platform, a gold-backed coin arrangement, and a platform where users could use the coin. Those are claims about products and services, not evidence in this record of a deposit demand, a guaranteed return, or a specified downline-income scheme. The account-based buying opportunity and invitation to show the coin to friends deserve scrutiny, but they do not by themselves show that viewers were required to pay or that referrals earned commissions. The available footage and transcript describe promotion, not the mechanics of a completed transaction.

a casino and a sports betting platform where all of you can play with your one coins.
What you can do the next coming weeks to show one point for your friends.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to promotional claims, but it does not show a payment request, a guaranteed return, a referral commission, or a credential request. The mention of mandatory accounts does not specify their cost or conditions. The phrase about showing the coin to friends is unclear in the transcript and does not establish a downline mechanism. Likewise, describing a gold arrangement is not independent proof that it was fulfilled, but lack of verification alone does not establish the transaction mechanics alleged.

citations.quote: There will be buying opportunities from the mandatory accounts.
What you can do the next coming weeks to show one point for your friends.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a transcripted deposit instruction does not erase the explicit buying opportunity, price, and claim that value will rise. The speaker also links the coin to network marketing and asks attendees to show it to friends. These are promotional signals; the defense's uncertainty about payment mechanics cannot turn the claims into ordinary commerce or establish that they were accurate.
